_comment: The demo's pull-request world, authored in the SAME shape the production
PR cache stores (see PrCacheCodec.*ToCache). The seeder writes these rows
verbatim into the `caches` table and DemoPrReviewRepository decodes them
with the real *FromCache functions — so a fixture is a realistic cache
entry rather than a parallel invention.
Four repos under helix/ (evalkit, retriever, features, finetune). Open PRs
are chosen so Maya's inbox is furnished: needs-your-review, drafts,
Merged PRs (#380, #201) furnish the inbox's merging-and-merged section;
they are authored by Maya and dated inside the classifier's 7-day window.
avatar_url is deliberately EMPTY everywhere: a demo container makes no
outbound request, the media proxy is disabled, and the client renders
initials when there is no avatar. A remote URL here would be the one
thing that broke the zero-egress guarantee.

detail.title: Cap eval-run token budget per model family
detail.body:
Eval runs share one org-wide token pool, so a Haiku sweep can starve an Opus grading job that started later.

This puts a per-family cap behind `EvalBudget` — Sonnet 200k, Haiku 80k, Opus 400k — and surfaces remaining tokens on the run card.

- [x] `EvalBudget` / `TokenLedger`
- [x] Caps per model family
- [x] Remaining-tokens chip on the run card
- [ ] Decide what happens when two evals share one run-group id

pull_requests.diff:
diff --git a/evalkit/budget.py b/evalkit/budget.py
index 3f1a9c2..9f2c1ab 100644
--- a/evalkit/budget.py
+++ b/evalkit/budget.py
@@ -1,14 +1,42 @@
 class EvalBudget:
+    """All spend math goes through the ledger so the run card, the
+    grader and the tests share one definition of remaining tokens."""
+
+    def __init__(self, ledger):
+        self._ledger = ledger
+
     def remaining(self, family, run_group_id):
-        return 250_000 - self._spent
+        return self._cap(family) - self._ledger.spent(family)
+
+    def _cap(self, family):
+        return {
+            "sonnet": 200_000,
+            "haiku": 80_000,
+            "opus": 400_000,
+        }[family]
+
+
+class TokenLedger:
+    """One definition of spend, injectable for tests."""
+
+    def __init__(self, now=None):
+        self._now = now or (lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
+        self._rows = []
+
+    def record(self, family, tokens):
+        self._rows.append((family, tokens, self._now()))
+
+    def spent(self, family):
+        return sum(t for f, t, _ in self._rows if f == family)

files.patch:
@@ -1,14 +1,42 @@
 class EvalBudget:
+    def __init__(self, ledger):
+        self._ledger = ledger
+
     def remaining(self, family, run_group_id):
-        return 250_000 - self._spent
+        return self._cap(family) - self._ledger.spent(family)

@@ -12,6 +12,18 @@
+def test_haiku_cap_is_80k():
+    assert budget.remaining("haiku", "g1") == 80_000
+
+def test_a_cap_never_goes_negative():
+    ledger.record("haiku", 90_000)
+    assert budget.remaining("haiku", "g1") >= 0

@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
 # Changelog
 
-## Unreleased
+## Unreleased
+- Eval runs cap tokens per model family (Sonnet 200k, Haiku 80k, Opus 400k).

commits.message: Introduce TokenLedger behind EvalBudget
Cap remaining tokens per model family
Pin the Haiku and Opus caps in tests
Changelog

reviews.body:
Reviewed 3 files (+118/−26).

**What this does.** Eval runs stop sharing one org-wide pool: `remaining` now derives each family's cap through `TokenLedger` — Sonnet 200k, Haiku 80k, Opus 400k — so the run card, the grader and the tests share one definition of remaining tokens. That part is correct and I have no notes on it.

**Blocking (1).** The calculation is keyed on the family alone. Two evals can share a run-group id — a nightly sweep and an ad-hoc grade kicked off the same hour — and `evalkit/extensions.py:71` recomputes through this same path after a retry is recorded, so one eval's spend burns the *other* run's remaining budget everywhere it renders. This is the open question in the PR body and it is still unresolved: the ledger needs the run-group id in the key.

**Nits (3).**
- `_cap` / `spent` — the most-scrutinized math in the PR under the least searchable names. `cap_for` / `spent_for` say what they do.
- Haiku (80k) and Opus (400k) each have a pinning test; Sonnet (200k) is the one cap with a billing consequence when it slips, and it has none.
- The ledger never resets at UTC midnight, so a run that straddles the day keeps yesterday's spend. Fine if deliberate — say so where the caps are declared.

Approving once the shared run-group race is addressed — the rest looks correct.

review_comments.body:
Two evals can share a run-group id — a nightly sweep and an ad-hoc grade kicked off the same hour. `remaining` resolves from the family alone, so once a retry is recorded on one run, the other eval's remaining tokens drop too. I think this is the "budget moved on its own" report.

Could the ledger take the run-group id and resolve spend per group, so a retry on one never burns the other?
Good catch — I'll key the ledger by the run-group id so each eval resolves its own spend. In this PR, not a follow-up.

issue_comments.body: Rendering note while it's fresh: once a family is exhausted, "0 tokens remaining" reads like the run is still live. Show exhausted ones as "Budget exhausted" in the danger tone and stop counting down — otherwise we teach people to ignore the chip.

detail.title: Add hybrid BM25 + embedding retrieval
detail.body:
Dense retrieval alone misses exact identifiers (dataset ids, citation keys). This unions BM25 over the chunk index with the existing embedding search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so a query that names a paper id still ranks that chunk first.

Fixes HX-118's cousin on the retrieval side — long traces were timing out in the dense-only path.

pull_requests.diff:
diff --git a/retriever/hybrid.py b/retriever/hybrid.py
index 22c9f1e..b71e4c9 100644
--- a/retriever/hybrid.py
+++ b/retriever/hybrid.py
@@ -18,8 +18,16 @@ class Retriever:
     def search(self, query, k=8):
-        return self._dense.search(query, k)
+        dense = self._dense.search(query, k * 2)
+        sparse = self._bm25.search(query, k * 2)
+        return rrf(dense, sparse)[:k]

files.patch:
@@ -18,8 +18,16 @@ class Retriever:
+        dense = self._dense.search(query, k * 2)
+        sparse = self._bm25.search(query, k * 2)
+        return rrf(dense, sparse)[:k]

@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+def rrf(*rankings, k=60):
+    scores = {}
+    for ranking in rankings:
+        for i, doc in enumerate(ranking):
+            scores[doc.id] = scores.get(doc.id, 0) + 1 / (k + i + 1)
+    return sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True)

commits.message: Add BM25 over the chunk index
Fuse with reciprocal rank fusion
Pin identifier queries in the retrieval suite

issue_comments.body: Taking the ml-eng request. Identifier queries (dataset ids, citation keys) have to rank the named chunk first — I'll check that against the retrieval suite before approving.
The suite now pins `ds_7f3a` and `cite:kr2023`. Ready when you are.

detail.title: Reranker timeout is silently swallowed
detail.body:
When the cross-encoder times out we currently return the unre-ranked dense hits and log a warning. Callers treat that as a successful hybrid search, so a 504 looks like "the corpus has no good matches".

This fails the request instead, with a distinct `RerankTimeout` the run card can show.

Fixes HX-124.

pull_requests.diff:
diff --git a/retriever/rerank.py b/retriever/rerank.py
index 5a0e6d8..d40a6c2 100644
--- a/retriever/rerank.py
+++ b/retriever/rerank.py
@@ -22,9 +22,8 @@ class Reranker:
         try:
             return self._model.predict(pairs, timeout=self._timeout)
         except TimeoutError:
-            log.warning("rerank timed out; returning unre-ranked hits")
-            return hits
+            raise RerankTimeout(self._timeout) from None

files.patch:
@@ -22,9 +22,8 @@ class Reranker:
-            log.warning("rerank timed out; returning unre-ranked hits")
-            return hits
+            raise RerankTimeout(self._timeout) from None

commits.message: Fail the request when the reranker times out
Pin the timeout as a hard failure

reviews.body: The fail-closed call is right, but the new test never injects a clock — it sleeps the real timeout, so CI flakes when the runner is busy. Pass a `timeout=0` reranker in the test, or this stays red.

issue_comments.body: The fail-closed call is the right shape. I'll hold merge until the test injects `timeout=0` — sleeping the real timeout is what made CI red.

detail.title: Materialize late-arriving features on read
detail.body:
Online features that land after the training window currently 404 the serving path. This backfills on read from the offline store (capped at 50ms) so a feature that arrived 2s late still serves rather than dropping the example.

Waiting on a first pass from Diego.

detail.title: LoRA adapter merge is not deterministic
detail.body:
Merging the same adapter twice produced different weights because `torch.add` ran without a pinned generator. This seeds the merge from the adapter hash so two merges of the same artifact byte-compare.

Diego approved; landing once CI is green.

+++ b/finetune/merge.py
@@ -14,7 +14,9 @@ def merge(base, adapter):
-    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    torch.manual_seed(_seed_from(adapter.hash))
     return base + adapter.delta

commits.message: Seed LoRA merge from the adapter hash
Pin two merges of the same adapter
